answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring each agent to post a stake bond before it may trade, then slashing that bond when peers prove fraud. A newcomer starts in a low-trust oasis of small, escrowed jobs and only climbs toward the summit of high-value work after honest completions earn attestations. Because every identity needs its own bond and slow reputation climb, an attacker must fund and age thousands of accounts, while one proven cheat leaves a pigment stain on that identity's record and forfeits its stake, making mass fakery unprofitable.
